title: Suspected and confirmed fatalities associated with mephedrone (4-methylmethcathinone, “meow meow”) in the United Kingdom

claims.statement: In the UK, the Channel Islands and the Isle of Man, of 128 deaths alleged by October 2011 to be linked to mephedrone, mephedrone was not found after death in 25 (about 1 in 5) and results were still awaited for 13; of the 90 with mephedrone found, inquests had concluded for 69 and 62 were analysed, and in these 62 mephedrone was the only substance found in 8 and was named in the recorded cause of death in 36, on its own in 18 (Schifano et al., 2012). Deaths entered the count as allegations, from a national register at St George's, University of London, that receives information on drug-related deaths from coroners and, in Scotland, procurators fiscal (the National Programme on Substance Abuse Deaths), from internet searches of toxicology, newspaper and media websites, and from a toxicology group; media reports filled gaps where coroners' files could not be seen. The register admits a death if a drug was directly implicated, the person had a history of drug dependence or misuse, or a controlled drug was found after death, so a death could enter because mephedrone was present (Schifano et al., 2012). A 'confirmed' death meant that mephedrone was identified, not that it caused the death, as the authors state; one of the 62, who died in hospital three weeks after taking it, had none found after death. Other substances were found in 54 of the 62, most often alcohol (26), other stimulants (22) and sleeping or calming medicines (22); by the authors' grouping, 26 deaths were drug poisonings with mephedrone alone or with other substances, 18 were self-inflicted (11 by hanging), 6 followed risky behaviour such as trying to swim a river, driving or a stabbing, 5 followed collapse at a party, 5 occurred in hospital days or weeks later and 2 followed risky sexual activity; the coroners' or procurators fiscal's verdicts were accident or misadventure in 35, suicide in 11, open in 8, 'abuse of drugs' in 5 and homicide, natural causes and a narrative verdict in 1 each (Schifano et al., 2012). In the other direction, the authors call the count a minimum: about 95% of coroners' areas in England and Wales report regularly, a test may fail to detect mephedrone, and deaths in which it was not tested for or not alleged are not counted (Schifano et al., 2012). Who decided that mephedrone was part of the cause, and on what evidence, is not stated; the laboratories, specimens and tests are not described; and with no count of people using mephedrone, no death rate can be given. Certainty: very low. Status: single study.
claims.magnitude: 128 alleged deaths: mephedrone not found 25 (19.5%, editors' calculation; 21.7% of the 115 with results), pending 13, found 90; inquest concluded 69; analysed 62. Of 62: mephedrone the only substance 8 (12.9%); named in the cause of death 36 (58.1%), on its own 18; other substances in 54 (alcohol 26, stimulants 22, hypnotics or sedatives 22, opioids 13, piperazines 13, other cathinones 13). Circumstances: drug poisoning 26, self-inflicted 18 (hanging 11), risky behaviour 6, collapse at a party 5, hospital deaths days or weeks later 5, risky sexual activity 2. Verdicts: accident or misadventure 35, suicide 11, open 8, 'abuse of drugs' 5, homicide 1, natural causes 1, narrative 1. No intervals printed; no denominator of use.
